clue.text: An eccentric person's single on account of the heart

parts.note: a card is an amusing, eccentric character
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: An oddball who stays single and blames it on a matter of the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing the account abbreviation after the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiac is the medical adjective relating to the heart muscle and its conditions.

clue.text: Is able to travel back after cold drink

indicators.note: after says the turned phrase follows the cold abbreviation

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: back means the phrase 'can go' is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: is able = can, to travel = go, giving 'can go'

explanation.surface: Someone recovers enough to set off home after a chilly drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Is able to travel back' as someone heading home; in fact 'back' reverses the phrase, and 'after' places it behind the cold letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, a strong spirit served as a drink.

indicators.note: in tells us the 'about' word sits inside the street word

parts.note: a road is a street
RE is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: Somebody was yelling while wandering about in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To roar is to bellow loudly, so it is a strong synonym for yelled.

clue.text: MP inside or possibly doing bird

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of 'MP inside or' could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament ends up behind bars, or might be locked up for a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing bird' is British slang for serving a prison sentence (from rhyming slang 'bird-lime' = time).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone doing bird is serving time in jail, that is, locked up as a prisoner.

indicators.note: in places the owing word inside the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
to be overdrawn is to owe the bank money

explanation.surface: A bank customer told to pull back, being overdrawn when they should be in credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to shrink back or recoil in fear, a kind of withdrawing.

clue.text: It's best one's embraced by plump mother

indicators.note: embraced by says the numeral is held inside the choosing word and the mother word

parts.note: to plump for is to opt, or choose
mum is an informal word for mother
I is the Roman numeral one; 's is short for 'is'

explanation.surface: A chubby mum hugs her child, and it's the best feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link; 'plump' looks like an adjective for the mother but is the verb, as in plumping for something.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the most favourable or ideal outcome or level.

clue.text: Open last of chianti before claret's drained

indicators.note: before says the chianti letter comes ahead of the claret word

parts.note: overt means open, not concealed

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word chianti

parts.note: claret is a red wine, so red

explanation.surface: A wine buff opens a Chianti before the claret has been emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtired means exhausted beyond the point of easy rest, worn out.

explanation.surface: Small measures for little ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Tots are small servings of spirits such as whisky, and also young children.

indicators.note: in places the colloquial word inside the premier word

parts.note: main means chief or premier
ain't is the colloquial or non-standard form of isn't

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister, speaking casually, is not giving support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premier' suggests the Prime Minister, but it simply means chief; the colloquial word splits the premier word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain someone is to provide for or keep them, giving them support.

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet
rates are speeds, as in the rate of travel

explanation.surface: A fighter plane picks up speed and lifts off the runway.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'takes off' is a looser definition: birds that migrate take off for other lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Migrating birds depart en masse, flying away to another region for the season.

clue.text: Catch breath swallowing last of beer

indicators.note: swallowing says the breath word takes in the beer letter

parts.note: a gasp is a sharp breath

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word beer

explanation.surface: Someone catches their breath after gulping the last of a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp is to seize or catch hold of something firmly.

indicators.note: in places the others-and-left pieces inside the faction word

parts.note: a wing is a faction of a party
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Squabbling breaks out as the rest walk away from a party faction.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrestling is a form of combat sport in which opponents grapple and fight.

clue.text: Better time with ale or a rum

indicators.note: rum here is the adjective meaning odd or strange, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Life improves with some time off, an ale, or a tot of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink after ale, but it is the adjective 'odd' signalling the anagram; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to improve or make something better, a verb sense.

indicators.note: backing means the stake word is read from end to start

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up in poker

explanation.surface: Betting money on an unpredictable horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' suggests a horse in the betting picture; it is a mountain, the active Sicilian volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is an active volcano in Sicily, a mountain whose eruptions cannot be foreseen.

clue.text: Most saucy, strangely saucier than removing article

indicators.note: strangely says the remaining letters are rearranged into an odd order
removing says the article letter is taken out of the words before the shuffle

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something is the cheekiest of all, oddly even more so than a saucier rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing article' drops one A from SAUCIERTHAN, leaving SUCIERTHAN (or SAUCIERTHN) for 'strangely' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Raunchy means sexually earthy or risqué, so the superlative is the most suggestive.

clue.text: He craves vote in new assembly

indicators.note: a new assembly of the letters of 'craves vote in' puts them together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A politician hungry for votes in a newly elected parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the definition: a person who supports the British right-of-centre party; the clue as a whole paints such a candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory is a man or woman belonging to the right-of-centre party, so 'he' stands for one.

parts.note: Jack Straw was a Labour cabinet minister, the UK's Home and Foreign Secretary
to poll is to cut short, as hair or the top of a tree

explanation.surface: A Labour MP slashes the ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is a major UK political party, so 'Labour politician' points to a well-known member.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw poll is an unofficial ballot taken to gauge opinion, an informal vote.

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a British cleaner
très is French for very

explanation.surface: A cleaner speaks of a town she finds terribly French.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'char' is a British term for a domestic cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres is a cathedral city southwest of Paris, a town in France.

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of big

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
to let is to allow or grant

explanation.surface: A conceited show-off gets a national award band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big-head' looks like a conceited person, but splits as the head (first letter) of 'big'; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental band worn round the wrist.

explanation.surface: Tough bargaining with Arab partners.
explanation.walkthrough: Arabs here are the horse breed, so dealing in them is literally trading horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd, tough bargaining is called this idiom, and literally it means dealing in steeds such as Arabians.

parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair, so its treatment is a styling at the salon rather than electric therapy

explanation.definitionFit: A styled arrangement of the locks is what a shock of hair receives at the hairdresser.

indicators.note: taking means the fantasy word takes the drug letter inside it

parts.note: a story is a fictional tale, a fantasy
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A fanciful flight of imagination brought on by drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight of fantasy' reads as one phrase, but 'Flight' alone is the definition and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is a level of a building, reached by a flight of stairs.

clue.text: 'Blue streak' going around the speed of light

indicators.note: going around says the streak word encloses the light-speed letter

parts.note: a ray is a beam or streak of light
c is the symbol for the speed of light in physics

explanation.surface: A blue flash races about at light speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' here means risqué or smutty, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes or films are indecent, and racy means suggestive in the same way.

indicators.note: change says the letters of 'where state' are altered into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A political question about where a state is stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steady' is the noun for a regular boyfriend or girlfriend, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is a regular romantic partner, which is what a beloved darling is.

indicators.note: embrace says the different word wraps around the numeral

parts.note: else means other or different
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A woman is one who prefers someone else's hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is short for 'is' and 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a female first name, so it stands for a woman.

indicators.note: topless says the first letter is cut from the hag word

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman, a witch

explanation.surface: An exclamation of lust at seeing an old crone without her top.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving or longing for something.

clue.text: Senator with endless lie about kin

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are rearranged
endless says the final letter of lie is dropped

explanation.surface: A senator with a never-ending fib about family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims lie to LI; 'about' shuffles SENATOR plus LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Relations are members of one's family, people related by blood.

clue.text: Queen takes bishop — first obvious mistake

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

indicators.note: takes says the bishop letters hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of obvious

explanation.surface: A chess blunder: letting the queen capture a bishop is an obvious error.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture is misleading; 'takes' has the bishop pair take in the O, the opening letter of 'obvious'.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a blunder or slip, a synonym for a wrong move.

clue.text: Textbook case in games at Chelsea

indicators.note: in says the letters lie concealed within the words games at Chelsea

explanation.surface: A schoolbag appears at sports matches in Chelsea.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a London district (and football club).
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a school bag that carries textbooks, so it is a case for them.

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
ropy is British slang for poor or terrible

explanation.surface: A hospital ward suffers a dreadful slump in standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ropy' is informal British for poor in quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Entropy is gradual decline into disorder, a running down of a system.
